rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most informative first experiment is to establish a clean, minimal baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) uses the simplest standard encoder (PCA-2000) on the primary modality (RNA) with the simplest profile setting. This gives a performance floor against which all other design choices (better encoders, multiprofile aggregation, image modality, fusion) can be measured. It is computationally cheap, well-understood, and isolates the RNA signal quality without confounding from additional modalities or complex aggregation. From this anchor, subsequent experiments can systematically test whether scvi/scgpt encoders, multiprofile aggregation, image modality, or multimodal fusion each add value, making the remaining 9 experiments far more interpretable.

The only completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) yielded a low accuracy of 48.5%, giving us a weak RNA baseline. The most critical uncertainty at this stage is whether the image modality carries useful predictive signal at all—if it does, multimodal fusion becomes a high-value direction; if it does not, we should concentrate remaining budget on improving RNA representations. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest single-variable comparison to the RNA baseline: it swaps modality while keeping profile setting (singleprofile) and encoder complexity (standard pretrained CNN) comparable. This isolates the effect of information source without confounding changes in aggregation, fusion, or encoder sophistication. With 8 experiments left, resolving whether image is a viable modality is the highest-information experiment before committing budget to multimodal or advanced-encoder configurations.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000, single profile) achieves 0.485 accuracy while image (ResNet50, single profile) only reaches 0.208, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. The key uncertainty is whether a learned nonlinear representation (scvi_n200) can meaningfully improve over the linear PCA baseline. This experiment (config_004: RNA only, single profile, scvi_n200) isolates the RNA encoder choice while holding profile setting constant, giving a clean A/B comparison against config_001. If scvi_n200 substantially outperforms PCA, it signals that investing in stronger RNA encoders (scgpt) and multimodal fusion around them is worthwhile; if it does not, PCA is sufficient and we should pivot to testing multiprofile aggregation or multimodal fusion. With 7 experiments remaining, resolving the representation question early is the highest-leverage use of the next slot.

Evidence: RNA-only models dominate (0.48-0.52) over image-only (0.21), and among RNA encoders, scvi_n200 (0.520) beats pca_n2000 (0.485) by ~3.5%. However, the scgpt foundation-model encoder is completely untested. Question: config_007 (rna_only, singleprofile, scgpt) is a clean single-variable comparison to config_004, isolating the effect of encoder choice (scgpt vs scvi_n200) while holding profile setting and modality constant. Why this is best: Establishing the encoder hierarchy is the highest-priority design decision because the chosen encoder will underpin all subsequent multiprofile and multimodal experiments. If scgpt substantially outperforms scvi_n200, it becomes the backbone for the remaining 6 experiments; if it does not, we can confidently anchor on scvi_n200 and pivot to testing profile/aggregation/fusion. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most impactful design axis before committing budget to more complex configurations.

Evidence: scvi_n200 singleprofile (config_004, acc=0.5203) is the best configuration so far, clearly outperforming pca_n2000 (0.4849) and scgpt (0.4106) among RNA encoders, and vastly outperforming image-only resnet50 (0.2079). The multiprofile dimension is completely untested for any encoder. Question: Does moving from singleprofile to multiprofile with simple avgpool aggregation improve upon the best single-profile scvi_n200 result? This isolates the effect of profile setting/aggregation on the strongest encoder. Why this is best: It is the most natural exploitation of the current best result (scvi_n200) along the most important untested axis (multiprofile). Using avgpool keeps the experiment simple, avoiding confounding from a more complex transformer aggregator. If multiprofile+avgpool helps, config_006 (transformer) becomes a logical follow-up; if it doesn't, we can pivot to multimodal or image-encoder exploration with the remaining 5 experiments. This maximizes information gain per experiment under the tight budget.

The current best result is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy, showing that multiprofile + scvi_n200 is a strong combination. The only untested dimension within this best sub-space is the aggregation method: we have avgpool but not transformer. Config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) is a clean single-variable comparison against config_005, isolating the effect of aggregation. This is critical because the aggregation choice will determine which multimodal multiprofile configurations (config_032/033 vs config_030/031) to prioritize in the remaining 4 experiments. Resolving whether transformer outperforms avgpool now reduces uncertainty for all downstream multimodal decisions and avoids wasting budget on a suboptimal aggregation strategy.

Evidence: RNA-only multi-profile with scVI n200 + transformer aggregation is the current best (0.653), and image-only ResNet50 is very weak (0.208). The key uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion can add any complementary signal on top of the strong RNA multi-profile baseline, or whether the weak image modality will dilute performance. This experiment (config_032: multimodal, multi-profile, scVI n200, ResNet50, transformer, concat) directly tests whether the best RNA configuration benefits from adding image features via simple concatenation. It is the most logical single extension of the current best setup, changes only the model setting (adding image + fusion) while keeping all other choices at their validated optima. If it fails to beat 0.653, we can confidently conclude image adds no value and spend remaining budget on RNA-only refinements; if it succeeds, it opens a productive multimodal direction for the final 3 experiments.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688 acc. The evidence strongly supports this architecture: scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder, multiprofile adds ~13% over single profile, transformer aggregation is marginally best, and multimodal fusion adds ~3.5% over RNA-only. The key remaining uncertainty within this top-performing family is the fusion strategy: concat vs. weighted. Config_033 is an exact single-variable comparison to config_032 (only fusion changes from concat to weighted), cleanly isolating whether learned or adaptive weighting of the two modalities outperform simple concatenation. With only 2 experiments left, this focused exploitation of the best-known architecture while resolving the fusion question is the highest-value next step. If weighted wins, the final experiment can push further (e.g., a better image encoder); if concat holds, we confirm the current best and can spend the last experiment on a different axis.

The current best (config_033, acc=0.7131) uses multimodal + multiprofile + scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted. The image modality contributed a meaningful +0.06 boost over RNA-only, but resnet50 is a relatively weak image encoder (0.21 standalone). The most promising unexplored dimension is upgrading the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l, a substantially more powerful pretrained model. config_039 changes only the image encoder (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) while keeping all other settings at their proven best values (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion), isolating the effect of image encoder quality. If a stronger image representation adds more complementary information, this could push past 0.7131. This is the highest-value single-variable extension of the current best, and if it succeeds, experiment 10 can further refine; if it fails, config_033 remains our strong baseline for the final experiment.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 accuracy. Evidence shows scvi_n200 > pca_n2000 > scgpt for RNA, imagenet_vit_l > resnet50 for image, weighted > concat for fusion, and multiprofile >> single profile. The only untested single-variable perturbation from config_039 that retains all other optimal components is config_037, which swaps transformer aggregation for avgpool. In the RNA-only multiprofile setting, the transformer-avgpool gap was minimal (0.6530 vs 0.6501), and we have no direct evidence of which aggregation is superior in the multimodal+imagenet_vit_l context. This experiment isolates the aggregation effect under the strongest image encoder, providing the highest expected accuracy among remaining options (only a ~0.003 expected drop) and confirming whether transformer aggregation's marginal benefit persists in the multimodal regime. As the final experiment, it maximizes the small probability of matching or exceeding 0.7250 while yielding a clean ablation of aggregation in the best-performing configuration.
